surface: The date editor, a native date input over the cell: opening it, typing a date, Enter committing it, and Escape cancelling a second edit.

steps.note: Enter opens the editor on the Start cell (`6/10/24`) and focuses its native date input, which holds 2024-06-10. Only the control's role is required, in whatever words the reader and the engine use: Chromium builds the input from month, day and year spin buttons, and Firefox and WebKit differ. The tree golden gives the input no accessible name, so no name is required; that is a finding candidate. Unsure of the segment the reader names first.

Eight digits fill the segments of the input: the digits are the same for month-day-year and day-month-year order (01/01/2020), which is why this date. Nothing is required: a reader speaks each segment's new value, and which words it uses depends on the engine. Unsure on Linux WebKit, which takes no typed digits in a date input (date-editor-keyboard-focus.spec.ts); the macOS VoiceOver lane has not been checked.
Enter commits the date and moves the selection one row down (enterMoves), so the cell announced is the next row's Start, 2024-01-05, drawn as `1/5/24` (en-US short date style).
ArrowUp returns to the edited cell, which now holds the typed date, drawn as `1/1/20`.
The editor opens again, on the new value.
Escape closes the editor without a change and the focus should return to the cell, which still reads `1/1/20`. Unsure: grid-core records that NVDA and VoiceOver say nothing here for the text editor.
